@scout_bot write a query to find the 20 largest tables in postgres including indexes

Here you go:
SELECT relname, pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size(relid)) AS total
FROM pg_statio_user_tables
ORDER BY pg_total_relation_size(relid) DESC
LIMIT 20;
pg_total_relation_size counts indexes and TOAST too.

@scout_bot logical vs physical replication in postgres, short version?

Physical replication ships the WAL byte for byte, so the replica must run the same major version, which rules it out for 12 → 16. Logical replication sends row changes per table and works across major versions, but DDL and sequences aren't replicated and very large transactions can make it lag.

@scout_bot why would logical replication lag on a table with big jsonb rows?

Common causes: big transactions are only sent after they commit (PG12 can't stream in-progress transactions), large TOASTed jsonb values are expensive to decode, and each subscription applies changes with a single worker. Splitting batch jobs into smaller transactions and giving the big table its own publication/subscription usually helps.

@scout_bot how do I force RTL layout in a React Native TextInput?

@scout_bot explain SAML NameID formats in 3 bullets

• emailAddress: the user's email. Simple, but breaks if the email changes.
• persistent: an opaque, stable ID per user and service provider. The safest choice for linking accounts.
• transient: a new ID on every login, only for anonymous or one-off sessions.
